target_customer: Hardware design teams, contract designers, hobbyists and students designing circuits and PCBs
problem: Electronics design tools were desktop, single user and isolated, which made collaboration, reuse of parts and design sharing hard.
business_model: Freemium SaaS with a paid professional tier (removed after the 2017 acquisition when it became free)
product_category: Browser-based electronic design automation and collaboration

founders.name: Stephen Hamer
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder with no bio. A funding article calls him CTO.

founders.name: Zak Homuth
founders.background_notes: Altium's acquisition announcement as reported by trade press names him CEO and co-founder; he is not on the YC page.

exit.reason: Altium announced the deal on 2017-08-28, brought in the whole engineering team including the CEO, and made Upverter free.

competitors.name: Eagle (CadSoft)
competitors.what: Desktop PCB design tool that was the hobbyist standard
competitors.traction_then: Adafruit and Sparkfun published all board files in Eagle format

competitors.name: Altium Designer
competitors.what: Professional desktop electronic design suite; Upverter pitched a free community edition against it

technical_complexity.rationale: A collaborative schematic and PCB editor running in the browser in 2011 needed real-time editing, a part library and file import from Eagle, Altium and OrCAD formats.

defensibility.rationale: A public library of designs (over 32,000 open source designs reported) and stored projects created some lock-in, but a closed web tool was criticized by open hardware advocates and free tools like KiCad existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Altium bought Upverter in August 2017 and in May 2018 announced CircuitMaker would become part of the Upverter product.

market_need_then: Hardware startups and makers were growing in 2011 and the available tools were single user desktop products; Hackaday framed Upverter as GitHub for hardware.

branding.domain_note: Used upverter.com; the domain did not resolve from this session's network.

identity.voice_and_tone: Collaborative, maker oriented; pitched as social making

branding.brand_signature: Positioned as the GitHub for hardware
branding.community_and_virality: Hackaday covered it in 2011 and later; a public library reached over 32,000 open source hardware designs. Some in the open hardware community called it a closed source vampire, per a secondhand blog account.

brand_strength.rationale: Repeated coverage on maker sites and a clear GitHub for hardware framing helped awareness, but the open source criticism limited goodwill.

outcome_analysis: Upverter built a browser-based circuit design tool, raised a small seed and then a 2.3 million dollar seed in March 2014, and was acquired by Altium in August 2017 with its team and CEO joining. The paid tier was dropped and the product was folded toward CircuitMaker in 2018, which suggests the standalone business had not reached venture scale. The sale price was not disclosed and the 2019 status of the product was not confirmed.
notes: Sources disagree on whether the 650 thousand and 2.3 million dollar figures are separate rounds; one profile lists two rounds totaling 2.5 million. The 650 thousand round has no date in the material I saw. Founder education and prior employers were not found. Eagle's 2011 position comes from a Hackaday snippet; its funding was not found.
